abstract_sentences.text: We study the problem of length generalization (LG) in transformers: the ability of a model trained on shorter sequences to maintain performance when evaluated on much longer, previously unseen inputs.

evidence.anchor: shorter sequences … much longer, previously unseen inputs

abstract_sentences.text: Prior work by Huang et al. (2025) established that transformers eventually achieve length generalization once the training sequence length exceeds some finite threshold, but left open the question of how large it must be.

evidence.anchor: left open the question of how large it must be

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we provide the first quantitative bounds on the required training length for length generalization to occur.

Motivated by previous empirical and theoretical work, we analyze LG in several distinct problem settings: ℓ∞ error control vs. average error control over an input distribution, infinite-precision softmax attention vs. finite-precision attention (which reduces to an argmax) in the transformer, as well as for one- or two-layer transformers.
In all scenarios, we prove that LG occurs when the internal behavior of the transformer on longer sequences can be “simulated” by its behavior on shorter sequences seen during training.
Our bounds give qualitative estimates for the required length of training data required for a transformer to generalize, and we verify these insights empirically.

These results sharpen our theoretical understanding of the mechanisms underlying extrapolation in transformers, and formalize the intuition that richer training data is required for generalization on more complex tasks.

claim_closure.claim: The minimum finite training length for single-layer finite-precision LG has a quantitative bound.
claim_closure.method_response: Hardmax token/position pattern is simulated by a shorter string z; Appendix A.2 gives count construction.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 4.1 and Eq. (2)–(29) provide the deterministic bound; Figures 1–3 only give qualitative support.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates parameter scaling and simulation principle.

claim_closure.claim: Average error can also length-generalize under a regular sequence distribution.
claim_closure.method_response: Suffix-aligned simulation, bulk concentration and Dirichlet lower-tail lemmas.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 4.2 plus Appendix A.3 provide proof; no independent average-case experiment.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion mentions average-error settings but leaves broader distributions future work.

claim_closure.claim: Infinite-precision depth-2 transformers admit a complexity/margin-controlled LG bound.
claim_closure.method_response: First-layer qf is bounded/Lipschitz in suffix and histogram; Lemma 5.3 preserves their joint empirical distribution.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 5.2 and Appendix B prove the restricted Fτ result; Figure 4 checks only S/k trends.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers depth/precision result without claiming larger depth.

claim_closure.claim: Richer training data is required for more complex tasks.
claim_closure.method_response: Complexity enters through L, Δ, |Σ|, τ, C(f), and margins.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Synthetic parameter sweeps are monotonic but do not identify a causal data requirement or test real LLMs.

claim_closure.claim: The simulation argument unifies finite- and infinite-precision analyses.
claim_closure.method_response: Finite case preserves hardmax frequency ratios; infinite case preserves suffix/histogram joint statistics via a probabilistic subset.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 4.1/4.2/5.2 proofs instantiate the two simulation maps.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion explicitly identifies simulation as the unifying high-level argument.

final_judgment.single_storyline: 将短训练长测试转成两个 limit transformers 的有限长度 agreement，并用保留 forward-pass sufficient statistics 的 simulation map 复原任意长度行为。Finite precision 通过 hardmax token ratios，infinite precision 两层模型通过 suffix/histogram joint distribution。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留 forward-pass、periodicity/locality/translation assumptions、Eq. (1)、三个 theorem、regime intuition、k-gram bridge、Figure 1–4 与未来边界。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A/B 承担 ratio construction、Dirichlet concentration、Markov-chain variance、Lipschitz bounds 与完整 proofs；Appendix C 承担实现参数和 expressivity sketches。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 同一 simulation principle 贯穿 precision/depth；机制图 Figure 3 直接检验 hardmax，参数扫描 Figure 1/2/4 检查方向性预测。
final_judgment.largest_gap: 确定性/平均-case theorem 与 synthetic qualitative curves 之间仍有距离；没有 C(f)、γ 的直接估计、tightness、baseline、置信区间或更深模型。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 先明确长短输入必须保留的 sufficient statistics，再让定理、机制图和参数扫描分别对应同一统计对象。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 适用于 forward pass 可归约为有限统计且能对齐 suffix/position 的 sequence model；任意分布、非局部位置机制、训练动态和更大深度仍需新理论。

method_theory_analysis.finite_precision_mechanism: For N≥2^{p/γ}, post-shift non-maximal softmax terms round to zero, yielding uniform average over argmax tokens.
method_theory_analysis.infinite_precision_mechanism: The log(i) suffix factor yields token-dominant, balanced and position-dominant regimes; q_f is bounded and Lipschitz in suffix/histogram inputs.

theorem_results.label: Theorem 4.1
theorem_results.assumptions: single-layer, τ-local, Δ-periodic, translation-invariant, p-bit finite precision
theorem_results.conclusion: N=O(max{2^{p/γ}, L²Δ⁷|Σ|⁶τ²/ε²}) gives all-sequence O(ε) agreement from length≤N agreement.
theorem_results.empirical_correspondence: Figures 1–3 qualitatively probe L/ω, Δ and hardmax.

theorem_results.label: Theorem 4.2
theorem_results.assumptions: iid categorical token sequences, P∼Dirichlet((α_s)), α0=min_s α_s
theorem_results.conclusion: N0=O~(ε^{−2−2/α0}) gives arbitrary-T average error O(ε^{1/2}); conditional min-probability version gives O(ε).

theorem_results.assumptions: Fτ restricted depth-2 infinite-precision transformer, no second-layer position, nonnegative φ, ||E_s||≤1
